stories.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
stories.synopsis: Mara wants her father to tell her the truth about 1887 without having to ask, but he would rather keep the lamp lit and the subject closed.

scenes.title: The storm glass
scenes.summary: The glass stays clear while the sea turns. She stops asking him and starts watching him.
scenes.content:
The storm glass had been clear all morning, which was how Mara knew her father was lying. He kept it on the sill of the lamp room where the light could get at it, a sealed bulb of water and crystals that was meant to cloud before weather, and it sat there as clear as a held breath while the sea went the colour of slate.

“It's a toy,” he said, when she asked. “Your grandmother's toy.” Elias did not look at it. He looked at the wick he was trimming, and the wick did not need trimming.

She had learned to read him the way she read the water: not by what moved, but by what refused to.

“Tobias saw a boat,” she said.

“Tobias sees a great many things.” The shears closed on nothing. “Go down and see to the bread.”

By four the glass had clouded, and he had not.

The sea had been grey since dawn, and the gulls kept to the lee of the tower as if they knew something the glass did not. He said nothing, which was its own kind of answer, and she filed it with the others.

She counted the steps the way her grandmother had taught her, not to know where she was but to keep her hands from shaking. The book lay open on the table, and the dates in it did not match the ones in the flour tin.

Below, the harbour lights came on one at a time, each one a small refusal of the dark. By the time the lamp was lit, the question had changed shape, and so had she.

dialogue.script:
MARA (pressing): It's clear.
ELIAS (correcting): It's a toy.
MARA (pressing): It was clear in March, too.
ELIAS (deflecting): Pass me the shears.
MARA (naming): You don't need the shears.
ELIAS (freezing out): …
MARA (retreating): Tobias saw a boat.

coreIdeas.title: Silence as care
coreIdeas.text: Truth withheld can be a kind of care, and it still costs. Nobody in this book lies to hurt.

coreIdeas.title: Inherited debt
coreIdeas.text: What the dead owed passes to the living whether they agree to it or not. The Board keeps the account; Nan kept the letters.

coreIdeas.title: The lamp
coreIdeas.text: Duty is a light you keep for strangers. It was the first thing the book believed, and it has gone quiet since chapter 1.
